name: Absolute humidity
seoDesc: Absolute humidity: work out your result from the relative humidity and the air temperature. A free physics calculator with the formula, units and a worked…
summary:
Supply the relative humidity and the air temperature and the Absolute humidity calculator solves for the answer. It is built for a lab report, a problem set or a sanity check on a physical situation.

Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Absolute humidity calculator work?
sections.html:
The Absolute humidity calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationships described below and reports every result it can derive from them.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the relative humidity and the air temperature.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.html:
• A number, expressed in %.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in Celsius. The unit chip switches it to any of the 28 supported units.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.
  • A plain number with no unit attached.

sections.title: The formula behind the Absolute humidity calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Critical temperature=-air temperature ÷ (tau − 1)
Critical temperature=100000000 × air temperature × temp water ÷ (180122502 × (tau ^ 15 ÷ 2) + 2268074110 × (tau ^ 7 ÷ 2) + 184408259 × (tau ^ 3 ÷ 2) − 1596187190 × (tau ^ 4) − 1178664970 × (tau ^ 3) − 785951783 × tau)
Sat vap pressure=critical pressure × the exponential of (temp water)
Actual vapor pressure=(1 ÷ 100) × relative humidity × sat vap pressure
Actual vapor pressure=(92302448913 ÷ 200000000) × absolute humidity × air temperature

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

  • Shown in pascals, and convertible to any of the 28 units on that chip.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Temperature, opening in Celsius
  • Pressure, opening in pascals
  • Pressure, opening in pascals
  • Density, opening in grams per cubic meter

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Absolute humidity calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Writing up a lab result and needing a quick cross-check
  • Solving a problem set where the algebra is more interesting than the arithmetic
  • Testing whether an answer is physically plausible before you trust it
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the relative humidity and the air temperature — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Absolute humidity calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The unit chips cover the units listed on the page. A historical or regional unit that is missing can still be used by converting it to a listed unit first.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Absolute humidity calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the relative humidity and the air temperature, which is 4 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter air temperature in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Air temperature opens in Celsius and the chip beside it offers 28 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Absolute humidity calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. The calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.
